title: Mathematics AI SL · Set A · Paper 1

questions.stem: A rectangular glass panel is recorded as 1.24 m by 0.86 m. Each length was rounded to the nearest 0.01 m.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the lower and upper bounds for the longer side, with appropriate inequalities.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A frame needs at least 1.060 m² of glass. Determine whether the recorded dimensions guarantee that it will fit this area requirement.

steps.text: Upper bound 1.245 m is excluded: 1.235 ≤ L < 1.245.
Use both lower bounds for the minimum possible area.
This is less than 1.060 m², even though the product of the recorded lengths exceeds 1.060.
No guarantee: some panels consistent with the measurements are too small.

questions.cognitiveDemand: Apply a model and interpret or justify its result in context.

questions.stem: In the first week of a trial a library issues 160 passes. In each subsequent week it issues 12 more passes than in the previous week.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the number issued in week 9.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the first week by the end of which the total number issued exceeds 2000.

steps.text: Sum the arithmetic sequence: S(n) = n[320 + 12(n − 1)]/2.
Week 10 is the first because the cumulative total strictly increases.

questions.stem: A cold-store probe gives a reading of 2.6 V at −4 °C and 5.0 V at 8 °C. Assume that voltage is a linear function of temperature over this interval.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the voltage model V = mT + c.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A reading of 4.3 V is observed. Estimate the temperature and explain why this is interpolation.

steps.text: The voltage lies between 2.6 and 5.0 V, the measured endpoints.

questions.stem: A rotating sprinkler waters a sector with radius 7.5 m and central angle 128°. Within the sector, water lands uniformly at 3.0 litres per square metre during one cycle.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the length of the curved outer edge.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A 190-litre tank is full. Decide whether it can supply one cycle, showing the unrounded calculation used to decide.

steps.text: Yes; approximately 1.50 litres remain, before any unmodelled losses.

questions.stem: Seven randomly selected morning journeys took 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 28 minutes. Use the median-of-halves convention, excluding the overall median.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the interquartile range and determine whether 28 is an outlier using the 1.5 × IQR rule.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A manager uses the sample mean to advertise a typical journey at any time of day. Give two distinct reasons for caution.

steps.text: 28 exceeds 23, so it is an outlier.
The long journey raises the mean relative to the median; the mean may be unrepresentative.
Only morning journeys were sampled, so other times of day are not represented.

questions.stem: A parcel desk processes 300 items: 180 are standard and 120 are express. Of the standard items, 9 arrive late; of the express items, 12 arrive late. One processed item is selected at random.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the item arrived late.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that it arrived late, find the probability that it was express.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine whether being express and arriving late are independent for these data.

steps.text: Restrict the denominator to the 21 late items.
This differs from 0.07, so the events are not independent.

questions.stem: For six bus stops the shelter length x (m) and the number y of seats are paired as follows: (2, 4), (3, 5), (4, 7), (5, 8), (6, 11), (7, 13).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use technology to find the least-squares regression line of y on x and the value of Pearson's r.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For the stop with x = 5, find the residual (observed minus predicted). Explain its sign.

steps.text: Enter paired data and select a linear regression predicting seats from length.
Predict at x = 5 using the unrounded fitted coefficients.
The actual stop has fewer seats than its fitted value.

questions.stem: At a loading bay, each crate independently has probability 0.12 of needing a second scan. A batch contains 18 crates.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that exactly two crates need a second scan.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Extra staff are called when three or more crates need a second scan. Find the probability of calling them, and explain why a change of scanner during a batch could invalidate the model.

steps.text: Use X distributed as binomial with n = 18 and p = 0.12.
Evaluate P(X = 2) using the binomial probability function.
The two scanners may have different second-scan probabilities, violating the constant-p assumption.

questions.stem: Two repair depots are located at A(1, 2) and B(7, 6), in kilometres. Travel is modelled by straight-line distance. The boundary contains points equidistant from A and B.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the equation of the boundary.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A new site C(6, 2) opens. A fault is reported at P(4, 3). Determine whether adding C changes which depot serves P.

steps.text: The slope of AB is 4/6, so the perpendicular slope is −3/2.
Compare squared distances from P to A and B.
PA² = 10 and PB² = 18, so A originally serves P.
C is closer than both original depots, so the assignment changes to C.

questions.stem: The amount of water in a tank is V(t) = 24 + 12t − 1.5t² litres, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the rate of change at t = 2, including units.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the maximum amount of water during the modelled period and justify that it is a maximum.

steps.text: t = 4 minutes, inside the stated interval.
The derivative is positive before 4 and negative afterwards (or the parabola opens down).

questions.stem: A co-operative borrows 9600 dollars. Interest is 6% nominal per annum compounded monthly. It makes 36 equal payments at the end of each month; there are no fees and the final balance is zero.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the monthly payment to the nearest cent.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the total interest paid to the nearest dollar, using the unrounded payment.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The co-operative considers 48 payments at the same rate instead. Compare the monthly payment and the total interest, explaining the difference.

steps.text: Use 36 end-of-month payments and present value 9600 with zero final value.
Principal is outstanding for longer, so interest accrues over more periods despite the smaller instalments.

questions.stem: Outflow from a sluice is measured every two minutes. At t = 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8 minutes the rates are 18, 25, 29, 26 and 20 litres per minute respectively.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the trapezoidal rule with all measurements to estimate the discharged volume.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A technician instead uses only the first, middle and last readings. Calculate the revised estimate and its percentage difference relative to the five-reading estimate.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why neither estimate establishes the exact volume.

steps.text: Width = 2 min; count each internal ordinate twice.
Interpolation between measured rates assumes straight segments; the true rate can follow a different curve.
